meta.about: The block as the running game built it: bounds, zones, every collider, the points the game flow and the AI use, the El and its train, the nav grid, and where every sign and window is.
meta.readFrom: the running web game (window.__G, three.js r160), every module real

units.web: metres, seconds, radians; +Y up, north = -Z, east = +X (right-handed)
units.ue: centimetres, degrees; +Z up, X = east, Y = south (left-handed)

meta.conversion: ue (X, Y, Z) = web (x, z, y) * 100; ue yaw = atan2(web z, web x) of a direction = -rotationY of a prop, in degrees

bounds.source: G.level.bounds (= G.physics.bounds): the play area and the extent of the nav grid; the ground is the plane y = 0

places.source: G.level.zoneName(x, z) sampled on a 0.1 m grid: the name the minimap band shows. The east zone ('lot') is THE CAGE north of the avenue, THE LOT south of it, THE AVENUE on the roadway between them.

ground.source: G.level.groundSurfaceAt(x, z) and G.level.floorAt(x, z) sampled on a 0.1 m grid. `surfaces`: what the bare ground plane is made of (footsteps, impacts; boxes standing on it report their own). `floors`: height of the level's own walking surface (0 the roadway, 0.15 a sidewalk slab).

playerStart.source: G.level.playerStart: feet position and heading (web yaw: 0 looks at -Z, positive turns left)

extraction.source: G.level.extraction: the zone behind the truck's rear doors; reaching it with all reels ends the mission
extraction.label: IPX truck

enemySpawns.source: G.level.enemySpawns (after the level moved blocked points to walkable cells). `facing` is NOT game data: the game keeps none and gives a new enemy a random yaw. It is derived here: a ground point looks toward the walkable nav cells it can reach in a straight line within 6 m ('opening'), an air point toward the middle of the block ('centre').

coverPoints.source: G.level.coverPoints: standing spots beside something solid that the Goons prefer as fire positions (config.json enemies.goon.cover, positionCost.cover)

explosives.source: G.level.explosives, with the state of the matching G.explosives.items entry. Rules per type: config.json explosives.kinds.

interior.source: G.level.interiorBoxes and G.level.interiorAt(pos): 1 inside a box, falling linearly to 0 over `fade` outside it (audio reverb, exposure). doorways: the openings the Buzzards fly in through, found by the AI itself (G.enemies.debug().doorways).

vantage.source: G.level.vantage: the scaffold shed in front of S3 (foot of its stair, a point on its deck)

cinematicPath.source: G.level.cinematicPath: the title fly-through, a closed loop through these held compositions (timing: config.json flow.titleCamera)

steam.source: G.level.steam: where steam rises (manholes, the alley, the lane, the dig's vent stack)

puddles.source: G.level.puddles: where water stands on the street (by day the street is dry outside the open hydrant's reach)

buildings.source: the solid buildings inside the bounds: footprint, wall material and storey count from src/level/layout.js BUILDINGS (imported in Node), roof height from its buildingHeight(), and the colliders the booted level tagged with the building's name (`parapetTop` is their top). `backs` are the neighbours' backs that seal the north, east and south edges, just outside the bounds.

el.source: deck: G.level.el. columns, girders, deckCollider, station: the colliders tagged el-column / el-girder / el-deck / station. layout: the constants of src/level/layout.js (EL, STATION), imported in Node.

train.source: config: G.config.look.train. tracks: src/atmos/plan.js trainTimeline() run in Node with the game's own bounds, speed, length and run-up, and checked against the durations the running game announced (train:pass). observed: the first two trains of this boot, timed on the atmosphere's clock (seconds of un-paused time since boot).
train.origin: the nose of the train is the moving point; the cars trail behind it; y is the rail top

schedule.rule: The first train starts so that its nose reaches the block `firstOverhead` seconds after boot; every later one starts `every[0]`..`every[1]` seconds (uniform) after the one before it started. Directions alternate, eastbound first. The clock stops while the game is paused.

nav.source: G.physics.nav: the occupancy grid the Goons path on (A* on cell centres, 8 neighbours, string-pulled). The rule constants are read from src/physics.js; the grid rebuilt from `colliders` with them equals the game's cell for cell.
nav.rule: cell (i, j) covers x origin.x + i*cell .. + cell and z origin.z + j*cell .. + cell. It is blocked when its centre lies within `inflate` of a collider that blocks nav: not noNav, not bulletOnly, not playerOnly, top at or above bandMin and bottom at or below bandMax. The outer ring is always blocked.

grid.rows: one string per row j (north to south), one character per cell i (west to east): # blocked, . free

physics.source: constants of src/physics.js, read from the source text (module-private): how a body moves over the colliders

colliders.source: G.physics.boxes, in the order they were added: every static collision box of the block (axis-aligned). tag: what the level calls it. owner: the placed prop (index into props.json instances) or the explosive (index into `explosives.items`) it belongs to, else the level itself. blocks: movement (bodies), shots (rays: rounds and sight), nav (stamped into the nav grid). A prop that stands at an angle is approximated by several boxes: `orientedBox` points at the true box in `orientedBoxes`.

orientedBoxes.source: every G.physics.addOriented call (heard by lib/hooks.cjs): the box as it was asked for, before it was sliced into axis-aligned pieces. All of them are prop colliders. extent = half size along the box's own X (length), Y (width), Z (height).

signage.source: paintings: every G.mats.sign / poster / graffiti / decal the level asked for (heard by lib/hooks.cjs). placements: the quads that carry them, read from the level's meshes (a quad of an atlas page whose texture rectangle is a painting's rectangle is that painting). right = reading direction, up = up the picture, normal = the side it shows. A tiling painting (road paint, a crosswalk) repeats along a quad of any length.

paintings.sub: OPEN 24 HRS  ·  COLD CUTS  ·  COFFEE  ·  LOTTO
EL STRUCTURE REPAIRS  ·  NO THRU TRAFFIC

paintings.text: SIDEWALK SHED  ·  PERMIT 0214  ·  STORES OPEN DURING WORK

placements.label: SIDEWALK SHED  ·  PERMIT 0214  ·  STORES OPEN DURING WORK

glazing.source: every flat four-cornered face of the level drawn with one of the catalogue's window glass materials (read from the merged level meshes). glass_lit_warm / glass_lit_cool glow at night (config.json catalog.MATERIALS); by day all of them are dark reflective glass. Car glass is part of the vehicle props and is not listed.

facades.source: wall faces that carry a painted window grid (G.mats.facade), read from the merged level meshes; the windows are placed with the painter's own layout (src/mats/layout.js facadeLayout, imported in Node). The grid repeats along the wall every `grid.width` and is bare wall above its top floor. state: dark | warm (a lamp-lit room) | tv (television blue): lit ones glow at night only.

layout.source: src/level/layout.js imported in Node: the table of footprints, heights and openings the level is built from. It is module data, not reachable from window.__G; the booted level is checked against it (bounds, zones, sidewalks, the El). Web metres; boxes are [x0, x1, z0, z1].
